entities.name: COPE
entities.notes: The body most publishers cite, unrevised since 13 February 2023. Its separate discussion document on AI in editorial decisions dates from September 2021, before ChatGPT was released. The position statement places a duty on authors and assigns them liability; it contains no instruction to editors on what to do with a disclosure once received. Live publicationethics.org returns 403 to automated clients, so this record is verified against a dated Internet Archive capture.

sources.note: Live publicationethics.org returns 403 to every automated client (Cloudflare). This is a dated Internet Archive capture of the same page. The corresponding live policy was re-read on 15 October 2026; fixed archive captures are retained as evidence and do not establish current live freshness.

policies.conditions: Methods placement, naming the tool — three years before ICMJE said the same. Note the scope: it already covers collection and analysis of data.

evidence.quote: Authors who use AI tools in the writing of a manuscript, production of images or graphical elements of the paper, or in the collection and analysis of data, must be transparent in disclosing in the Materials and Methods (or similar section) of the paper how the AI tool was used
Authors are fully responsible for the content of their manuscript, even those parts produced by an AI tool, and are thus liable for any breach of publication ethics.

policies.conditions: The statement explicitly extends to "the collection and analysis of data".

evidence.quote: Authors who use AI tools in the writing of a manuscript, production of images or graphical elements of the paper, or in the collection and analysis of data, must be transparent in disclosing in the Materials and Methods (or similar section) of the paper how the AI tool was used

entities.name: Elsevier
entities.notes: Rewrote its journals policy in June 2026, permitting reviewers supportive use of private AI tools. Its BOOKS policy previously used a URL ending 'in-the-review-process' and forbids editors using AI to evaluate material — secondary sources routinely quote that page as if it were the journals policy. Cell Press, an Elsevier imprint, is reported to serve superseded 2023 wording; Cell Press is not yet a record here. Re-read on 2026-09-11 against the text signed off on 2026-08-21: the record had captured five axes of a policy that rules on ten. Added writing, research-process, explanatory-image, data-visualisation and passing-off axes with quotes, and the 18 August 2026 Elsevier Connect announcement as a source.

sources.note: The slug says 'review process' but the page is Elsevier's BOOKS policy (13 mentions of book/chapter, zero of 'journal' in lower case). Secondary sources routinely quote it as if it were the journals policy. It is not. Recorded until 2026-09-11 as https://www.elsevier.com/about/policies-and-standards/the-use-of-generative-ai-and-ai-assisted-technologies-in-the-review-process, which now redirects here.
Elsevier Connect post announcing the updated journals policy, dated 18 August 2026; the policy page itself states 'Policy updated June 2026'.

policies.conditions: Exemption is withdrawn where changes go beyond basic correction. Specialist disability-related assistive technology used solely for accessibility is also exempt.

evidence.quote: Basic checks of grammar, spelling and punctuation do not need a declaration statement

policies.conditions: Output must be checked by a competent bilingual human.

AI tools may therefore only be used in a supportive capacity, for example to improve the language and structure of a review report, or to assist with a background literature search

evidence.quote: Through Elsevier’s editorial systems, editors have access to private AI tools that assist them in performing certain tasks, such as identifying relevant reviewers, matching the scope of submissions to their journal, and detecting duplicate submissions.

policies.conditions: No threshold for triggering review, no duty to notify the author, and no route of appeal is stated. The quote records what is granted instead: editorial discretion.

policies.conditions: Author-facing policy mentions image forensics only. Check Integrity was expanded to nearly 2,000 journals in March 2026 without appearing in the author policy.

Separate AI declaration statement at submission, published with the article; basic grammar and spelling checks exempt, substantive changes to structure or content must be declared. Output must not replace the authors' own judgement, analysis or interpretation.

evidence.quote: Authors should disclose the use of AI tools for manuscript preparation in a separate AI declaration statement included in their manuscript upon submission.
Although AI tools may support your writing process, they must not replace your own scientific judgement, analysis, interpretation or intellectual contribution.

policies.conditions: Research-method use must be reproducibly described in Methods. The author guidance also names agents and deep research tools for manuscript preparation.

evidence.quote: Where the use of AI tools forms part of the research design or research methods, the use of the tools must be described in a reproducible manner in the Methods section.

policies.conditions: Explanatory images only (flow charts, decision trees, timelines, schematic illustrations, workflow diagrams); tool, version and use disclosed in each caption and in the AI declaration.

evidence.quote: Authors may use AI tools to support the creation of certain types of explanatory images for publication, such as flow charts, decision trees, timelines, schematic conceptual illustrations, or experimental workflow diagrams.
The use of AI tools should be disclosed in the caption of each image (including the specific tool, version, and how the tool was used) and in the general AI disclosure statement in the article.

policies.conditions: Only where the visual is directly derived from underlying data via reproducible methods reported in Methods; tool, version and developer disclosed there.

evidence.quote: AI tools may be used to support the creation of data visualizations only when the visual output is directly derived from underlying data.
Where AI tools are used in the generation of data visualizations, authors should disclose the name of the model or tool, the version used, and the developer or manufacturer, in the Methods section.

policies.conditions: Covers fabricated results, invented or altered data, figures not faithfully derived from data, and primary research images (microscopy, blots, scans, patient images).

evidence.quote: AI tools must not be used to fabricate results, invent or alter underlying data, or generate figures that are not faithfully derived from the underlying data and methods used in the research.
AI tools must not be used to create or alter images that represent primary observed or experimental data that were not directly obtained in the research.

metadata_inconsistency.summary: The policy page's own footer states 'Policy updated June 2026', while Elsevier Connect announced 'Elsevier has updated its generative AI policies for journals' on 18 August 2026. Editorial-tool wording changed between the 15 October adjudication and 1 November snapshot while the stated update remained June 2026. This is an observed interval, not an inferred effective date.
